---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Moisture Recycling (Rainfall Pattern Regulation)"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Rainfall pattern regulation values the crop output supported by vegetation-derived moisture.
The quantity is Shunkei's VMR share of crop water satisfaction — the part of the water a crop
actually received that vegetation-regulated rainfall supplied — valued on the corrected 2019
commercial crop-provision basis in the water_supply run, and reported AT THE RECEIVING COUNTRY,
the agreed paper approach. The base year is 2019.

⚠ The published headline is an **intermediate contribution already inside crop provision, never
an addition to it** — the same convention as agricultural water, whose basis it shares. The
earlier construction (the water-supply irrigation and domestic GEP re-attributed to supplying
countries) is RETIRED and is not published under any name; the sink-fraction machinery now
serves only the source-side diagnostic below, whose source and sink totals agree by
construction, and the task raises if they differ.

## Quantity

The WAM2layers country-to-country sink-fraction matrix (Bakels and Wang-Erlandsson): cell
$[i, j]$ is the fraction of column-country $j$'s 2019 precipitation that evaporated from
row-country $i$'s land. A column sums to $j$'s terrestrial-origin share, below one because the
remainder comes from the ocean. Read from the path recorded in `es_parameters.csv` as
`moisture_recycling_sink_fraction_input_path`. Twelve destinations sit below the 0.5 degree
tracking grid and carry all-NaN columns; their water value goes unattributed and the task names
them and it.

## Price

None of its own. The value is the water_supply run's VMR crop components by receiving country
(`water_use_rainfed_vmr_gep` and `water_use_irrigated_vmr_gep`), read from the LIVE water table:
an explicit `moisture_recycling_water_gep_path` wins, else
`moisture_recycling_water_gep_relative_file` against the project directory, so the figure is as
fresh as the last water_supply run and a stale copy cannot shadow it. The component columns are
configuration (`moisture_recycling_water_gep_component_cols`).

## Attribution

`moisture_recycling_ecosystem_share` scales the terrestrial evaporation credited to ecosystems.
It is 1 in `es_parameters.csv`, counting all terrestrial evaporation; the transpiration-share
decision that would lower it is open with the group.

## Valuation

The headline is the receiving country's own VMR crop value: the two component columns summed per
country, a country missing both staying missing.

The source-side DIAGNOSTIC beside it runs the same value through `reattributed_water_value`:

$$
\text{GEP}_i = s \sum_j M_{ij} \, V_j
$$

where $M$ is the sink-fraction matrix, $V_j$ is destination $j$'s VMR crop value, and $s$ is the
ecosystem share. The diagonal term is the own part (a country's moisture serving its own crops)
and the rest the export part, with the destination-side view published as
`moisture_recycling_sink_side_value`. The diagnostic answers where the value WOULD go if
attributed to the countries whose evaporation supplied the rain; the headline stays at the
receiver.

`collapse_countries_to_r250` reduces the r264 correspondence to one canonical row per country
before the join, and the published table carries every account country, NA where the matrix has
no row.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in
constant 2019 USD. Of the 250, 138 carry a value and 112 are missing, kept as missing rather
than zero — the VMR pair is a subset of the agricultural water coverage (143), because five of
its countries carry lambda components with no VMR observation. A zero means the computation
returned zero; a missing row means the data to compute one is absent.

## Inputs

All paths and parameters come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `moisture_recycling` service key:
the sink-fraction matrix, the water-supply snapshot it re-attributes, the component column list,
and the ecosystem share, each with a source row beside it.
